question:
An astronomical telescope is pointed at a distant star and its objective forms a real image on a photoelectric detector placed at the focal plane of the objective.

Two telescopes $T_1$ and $T_2$ observe the same star under identical conditions. Their objectives have the same focal length, but different aperture diameters: $D_2=2D_1$.

The starlight reaching Earth may be treated as monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda=450\,\text{nm}$. The photoelectric detector has work function $\phi=2.0\,\text{eV}$. In both setups, the detector is operated under saturation conditions (anode sufficiently positive).

Assume:
1) The collected optical power is proportional to objective area $\propto D^2$.
2) The photoelectron emission rate (and hence saturation current) is proportional to the incident optical power.
3) Stopping potential depends only on photon energy.

If the stopping potential measured with $T_1$ is $V_s$, and the saturation photocurrent measured with $T_1$ is $I_{s1}=1.2\,\mu\text{A}$, find the stopping potential measured with $T_2$ and the saturation photocurrent $I_{s2}$ measured with $T_2$. Use $hc=1240\,\text{eV}\cdot\text{nm}$.
